items.title: Monitor data freshness in Lakeflow Connect database connector pipelines (Public Preview)
items.text: You can now see how current each destination table is in Lakeflow Connect database connector pipelines, in Public Preview. The new Data freshness column in the pipeline's tables list shows the time since the latest source commit that the pipeline ingested for each change data capture (CDC) table. Data freshness is available for SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Oracle sources. You can also query data freshness and end-to-end lag from the ingestion pipeline's event log, and create alerts on them. See Monitor data freshness for change data capture (CDC) tables.

items.title: Data quality monitoring anomaly detection is now generally available
items.text: Anomaly detection for data quality monitoring is now generally available. Enable it at the schema level to monitor the freshness and completeness of every table in the schema, based on historical data patterns. Results for all monitored tables are stored in the system.data_quality_monitoring.table_results system table, which is also now generally available. See Anomaly detection.

items.title: Announcing support for Materialized views and streaming tables in Mirrored Azure Databricks catalog
items.text: Sections: What's new; Why this matters; Prepare objects for external access; Work with data in Fabric; Keep catalog changes in sync; Get started. Access more Unity Catalog objects through the existing mirrored catalog experience in Microsoft Fabric We are expanding Mirrored Azure Databricks catalogs in Microsoft Fabric to support materialized views and streaming tables alongside tables. These objects remain created and managed in Azure Databricks, while Fabric provides read-only access to the underlying data through shortcuts. This brings more of your Unity Catalog environment into Fabric without copying or replicating the data. A Mirrored Azure Databricks catalog can now include support: Tables Materialized views Streaming tables When configuring the mirrored catalog, select the Unity Catalog catalogs, schemas, and supported objects you want to make available in Fabric. items.title: OneLake: The file system for agent-first data engineering
items.text: Sections: Managing OneLake; Querying OneLake; Discovery API example; From one prompt to your data. Software engineers are increasingly using agents to build software, and data engineers are no different. We want OneLake to help enable data engineers to develop software in this new agent-first era. Think about how you work in a terminal: you use it to run programs that read and write files. Both the programs and the data live in the file system. Now apply that model to data engineering: OneLake is the file system, Fabric engines are the programs, and the AI prompt is your terminal. Over the last few weeks, we’ve released several new capabilities in OneLake that come together to create an experience where agent-first data engineers can thrive. This blog post provides a rundown of those features. OneLake now offers a remotely hosted MCP server (preview), so agents can explore and manage your data without installing a local server.
